candidate_evidence.quote: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and feasibility of focused ultrasound (FUS)-mediated blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption using the Next Generation Dome Helmet (NGDH) in adults with glioblastoma (GBM) undergoing the maintenance phase of the standard "Stupp protocol".

At the time of each FUS session, participants will receive their prescribed standard of care TMZ dose, as well as an intravenous injection of DEFINITY® ultrasound contrast agent that enables targeted BBB opening.

candidate_flag.reason: Temozolomide (established GBM therapy) is paired with FUS-enabled BBB opening; could be read as a device-dependent candidate under C12/R5 rather than established_therapy_experiment.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Previously undergone a maximal safe surgical resection and completed concurrent, standard-of-care RT and TMZ without any complications and deemed eligible for the maintenance phase of TMZ treatment.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Blood samples will be analyzed for BBB disruption and tumour-related biomarkers, including S100β protein, inflammatory cytokines, circulating DNA, exosomes, and circulating tumour cells.

coder_notes: Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but every patient receives SOC TMZ at each FUS session (R9), so listed. The record's question is safety/feasibility of FUS BBB disruption during TMZ maintenance; keywords mention drug/chemotherapy delivery. Since TMZ is a D6 established GBM therapy, coded established_therapy_experiment (rule 6 exception i) rather than candidate; adjudicator should decide vs C12/R5 device-dependent candidate. device_dependent left false because the agent is not coded as a candidate. Target engagement coded no: blood biomarkers relate to BBB disruption, not to a candidate. Gadolinium mentioned only in exclusions, not listed.
